title: Identity Model v2 — Compound-Key Architecture & Registry Specification
sources: knowledge/DEFECT_LIBRARY.md (DL-008, DL-010, DL-012, DL-016, DL-018, DL-021, DL-025, DL-026, DL-028, DL-029, DL-030)
pack_d_corrected.js (AD-001 through AD-005 rotation group, lines 1-260)

compound_key.principle: A QID is a template-group identifier, not a unique item instance. Uniqueness within the pool requires the full compound key. No tool, scanner, or remediation script shall identify items by QID alone.

fields.purpose: Base template-group identifier — the human-readable label and file-scope namespace boundary.

pack_a.note: Section E uses this format within pack_a. Section letters are capital A-F. NNN is 001-150.

pack_b.note: Prefix 'P1B' distinguishes from Pack A's P1- format. CC stored BEFORE QID in JSON — unique to Pack B.

pack_c.note: Section letter + 'C' suffix for Pack C items. Older items may lack the C suffix (P1-BC-094 vs P1-AC-001). The C or lack thereof is the discriminator.

pack_d.note: Section letter + 'D' suffix for Pack D items. Shares template families with Pack C (same choice texts, rotated CC).

pack_e.note: Prefix 'P1E' distinguishes from Pack A's P1- format. Independent authorship pipeline — different template engine, no rotation groups.

cross_pack_collision_risk.scenario: Pack A Section E items use P1-E-NNN while Pack E items use P1E-E-NNN — visually similar but structurally distinct by prefix (P1- vs P1E-). No actual collision.
cross_pack_collision_risk.resolution: File_Path component of compound key disambiguates. P1-E-042 belongs to pack_a_corrected.js. P1E-E-042 belongs to pack_e_corrected.js.

cross_pack_collision_risk.scenario: Pack C and Pack D items share the same template families (stem skeleton, choice texts). P1-EC-001 in Pack C and P1-ED-001 in Pack D are template siblings but belong to different packs. QID format embeds pack identity (EC vs ED). No collision by QID alone, but Template_Family and File_Path add defense-in-depth.
cross_pack_collision_risk.resolution: Section suffix (EC/ED) embeds pack identity. File_Path is defense-in-depth.

fields.purpose: Distinguishes rotation positions within a template family. The CC value determines: (a) which EW slot must be empty (DL-008 governance), (b) which learner-facing choice letter is marked correct, (c) which distractor positions are expected to have non-empty EW text.
fields.validation: Must equal exactly one of A, B, C, D. Must not be empty, undefined, or multi-character.
critical_for: DL-008 detection — EW[CC] must be empty. If CC is read from the wrong item, the wrong EW slot is flagged.
DL-026 detection — non-CC EW slots must be non-empty. If CC is wrong, the emptiness signature is misread.
DL-030 detection — independent CC verification. If CC is wrong, the answer key is wrong.
S320 remediation — targeting the correct item variant in a rotation group. CC distinguishes AD-002 (CC=B) from AD-004 (CC=D) which share the same stem skeleton.

fields.purpose: The binary fingerprint of ExplanationWrong slot emptiness — the most reliable structural identity discriminator. Independent of CC value, stem text, and choice text. A bit-position change means a structurally different item.
fields.encoding: Position 0 = EW_A, Position 1 = EW_B, Position 2 = EW_C, Position 3 = EW_D. '0' = empty ('' or absent), '1' = non-empty.
significance: Rotation position discrimination: In a 5-item group with CC rotation A→B→C→D→A, the EW_Pattern for CC=A is '0111' (A empty, B/C/D non-empty), CC=B is '1011', CC=C is '1101', CC=D is '1110'. These are unique within the group.
DL-008 presence: A '0' at the CC position is correct (DL-008 compliant). A '1' at the CC position is DL-008 defect.
DL-026 presence: A '0' at any non-CC position is DL-026 defect (missing distractor explanation).
DL-021 presence: An absent field at any non-CC position is DL-021 (worse than empty).

Remediation targeting: A remediation script filling EW_B on CC=A item must verify EW_Pattern is '0111' before writing. If EW_Pattern is '0011' (DL-026), the script must author new text, not reuse existing text.

edge_cases.absent_vs_empty: Absent ('undefined') and empty ('') both encode as '0' in the pattern. A separate field-level check distinguishes DL-018 (absent CC slot) from DL-008 (non-empty CC slot) and DL-021 (absent non-CC slot) from DL-026 (empty non-CC slot). The binary pattern treats both as '0' for structural identity but the field-presence audit differentiates them.
edge_cases.dl013_boilerplate: DL-013 fields are technically non-empty ('1' in pattern) but contain boilerplate. The EW_Pattern alone cannot distinguish boilerplate from substantive text. Gate 2 content scan augments the pattern with semantic analysis.
edge_cases.dl010_misassignment: DL-010 fields are non-empty but describe the wrong choice. The EW_Pattern shows '1' at the correct structural position but the text is semantically wrong. Requires Gate 2 semantic verification.

fields.purpose: Identifies which rotation group this item belongs to. Items in a family share the same stem skeleton, the same four choice texts (positionally rotated), and the same ExplanationCorrect text. Only the company name and CC rotation distinguish family members.

identification_method.step_1: Parse all items in a section. Compute stem Jaccard similarity between all pairs after removing proper nouns (company names: Alderway, Bramblewood, Castlebrook, Deepwater, Elmsworth, Ashford, Brightpoint, Cedarline, Driftwood, Emberton, etc.).
identification_method.step_2: Group items with Jaccard similarity > 90% after company-name removal. These form a candidate template family.
identification_method.step_3: Within each candidate family, verify all items share the same four choice texts (only positionally rotated). Extract the canonical choice set: e.g., {A-text: 'sale of receivables', B-text: 'loan collateralized', C-text: 'reduction of revenue', D-text: 'increase to AP'}.
identification_method.step_4: Verify CC cycles through A, B, C, D, (A) across family members. A family of 5 items should have CC distribution A+B+C+D+A (2:1:1:1, 3 distinct letters, or other rotation patterns depending on family size).
identification_method.step_5: Verify company names follow a fixed alphabetical progression (e.g., Alderway→Bramblewood→Castlebrook→Deepwater→Elmsworth). This progression is the rotation-template artifact.
identification_method.step_6: Assign a canonical family identifier: {Section}_{concept}_{number}. Example: 'AD_factoring_001' for Pack D Section A factoring group 1. Save the family identifier to all member items.
identification_method.step_7: Identify the canonical seed: the item with the longest, most standard-referenced ExplanationCorrect (preferably with ASC/COSO citation), all EW slots substantive (no DL-013/010/026), and question_state: 'Unprocessed' or 'In Audit'. If no seed meets criteria, the family requires re-authoring.

family_size_distribution.typical: 5 items per family (1 seed + 4 clone siblings). The template engine generated 5 variants with company-name substitution.
family_size_distribution.variants: Some families may have fewer items due to prior archival or remediation. The Template_Family field tracks group membership regardless of family size.
family_size_distribution.clone_determination: An item is a clone if, compared to the canonical seed: (a) stem differs only by company name, (b) all 4 choice texts are identical (positionally rotated), (c) ExplanationCorrect is identical or nearly identical (Jaccard > 95%).

canonical_seed_criteria: question_state: 'Unprocessed' or 'In Audit' (not Archived, not already Certified if family is being re-evaluated)
ExplanationCorrect contains an explicit ASC, COSO, IAS, or IMA standard citation
All 3 non-CC EW slots have non-empty, choice-specific text (no DL-013 boilerplate, no DL-010 misassignment, no DL-026 empty slots)
DifficultyScore matches cognitive demand of the item (not inflated — DL-031 check)
Bloom's CognitiveLevel matches the cognitive demand implied by the stem
fields.clone_archival_rule: Non-seed clones should be Archived (question_state: 'Archived') unless they offer genuine pedagogical differentiation beyond company-name substitution. Clone items inflate the pool with zero additional testing value (DL-012: 140 clones across Pack C/D Section E).

fields.purpose: Disambiguates which pack file and section the item resides in. QID format alone is not globally unique. This field also determines scanner methodology (Pack B: CC-before-QID requires within-object extraction).
examples: pack_d_corrected.js:Section A — External Financial Reporting Decisions
pack_b_corrected.js:Section B — Planning, Budgeting, and Forecasting

scanner_implications.pack_b: CorrectChoice BEFORE QuestionID in JSON object. ALL scanners must use within-object extraction. Forward-scan from QID produces 100% false positives for CC-dependent checks.
scanner_implications.packs_a_c_d_e: CorrectChoice AFTER QuestionID. Standard within-object extraction works. Forward-scan produces ~25% false positives from boundary-crossing (missed QID or grabbed neighbor).
scanner_implications.pack_a_dual: Pack A items carry both metadata and content fields in a single JSON object. The 'dual-block' concept is a field-level organization pattern, not separate JSON objects. EW text and Choices text MUST be verified from the SAME object boundary. Cross-object EW-Choice pairing is invalid.

fields.type: String (UUID v7 or ISO-8601-derived timestamp + increment)
fields.purpose: Tracks content changes across certification waves. When any learner-facing field changes (Stem, Choices, CC, EC, EW[A-D]), the VersionID increments. This enables delta review: unchanged items skip re-review.
fields.format: YYYYMMDDHHMMSS-{increment} (e.g., '20260723144421-1') or UUID v7. The timestamp-increment format is human-readable and sortable; UUID v7 is more robust for distributed systems.
versioning_rules: Content change (Stem, Choices, CC, EC, EW[A-D]) → VersionID increments. New hash generated.
Metadata change (Difficulty, CognitiveLevel, question_state, LOSTag) → VersionID does NOT change. Metadata_Hash updates instead.
Structural fix (EW[CC] cleared from 'text' to '') → VersionID increments. The EW field changed. Hash changed.
No change → VersionID unchanged. Hash match confirmed.

lineage.parent_version: The VersionID of the item at the time of last certification. Tracked in CERTIFICATION_LEDGER.json.
lineage.replacement_lineage: When an item is superseded (e.g., re-authored from scratch with new QID), the old item is Archived and the new item inherits a lineage reference to the old QID. Format: {new_QID}.lineage = {old_QID}@{old_VersionID}.

compound_key_example.File_Path: pack_d_corrected.js:Section A — External Financial Reporting Decisions

canonical_choice_texts.A: As a sale of receivables, removing them from the balance sheet and recognizing any loss on sale
canonical_choice_texts.B: As a loan collateralized by receivables, with no change to the receivables balance
canonical_choice_texts.C: As a reduction of revenue for the period
canonical_choice_texts.D: As an increase to accounts payable

rotation_group_example.stem_skeleton: {Company} sells its accounts receivable to a factor without recourse. How should this transaction generally be recorded?
rotation_group_example.ec_text: A factoring transaction without recourse, where the factor assumes the risk of collection, is recorded as a sale of receivables, removing them from the seller's books.
rotation_group_example.note: AD-001 and AD-005 have identical EW_Pattern ('0111') and CC ('A'). They are structurally equivalent variants — company-name + Topic number (A.001 vs A.005) are the only differentiator. AD-001 is the canonical seed (longest EC, ASC 860 citations in EW slots, substantive distractor text). AD-005 is a clone.

template_rotation.description: Template engine produces N variants of the same stem skeleton where CorrectChoice cycles through A→B→C→D→(A) across variants. Company names progress alphabetically. The compound key disambiguates each variant.
template_rotation.compound_key_role: QID identifies the template group. CorrectChoice discriminates which variant this is (position in the rotation cycle). EW_Pattern confirms structural identity. Template_Family groups all variants for cross-item audit.
template_rotation.s320_prevention: A remediation script must match on QID + CorrectChoice + EW_Pattern + question_state simultaneously. The script identifies P1-EC-001 with CC=A and EW_Pattern=0111 and question_state='Unprocessed' — not the first brace-matched occurrence of 'P1-EC-001' which might have CC=B.
template_rotation.canonical_seed_selection: Within a family, the canonical seed is the item with the most substantive content (EC length, standard citations, EW quality). All other family members are clones. Seed selection must verify: CC matches EW_Pattern (CC-slot empty), EW non-CC slots are all non-empty + choice-specific.

remastering.description: An existing Certified item's content is changed (Stem rewritten, Choices updated, EC expanded, EW slots filled). The item retains its QID but gets a new VersionID.
remastering.compound_key_role: QID, CorrectChoice, EW_Pattern, Template_Family, and File_Path remain stable (identity components). Only VersionID increments. The item's content_hash changes but its compound key (minus VersionID) stays the same. Delta review detects the hash change and routes to full Quality Board review.
remastering.certification_continuity: The item's question_state transitions: Certified → In Audit (re-verification) → Certified (with new VersionID). The CERTIFICATION_LEDGER appends a new entry with the new VersionID, linking to the previous version via parent_version.

replacement_lineage.description: An item is replaced by a completely new item (new QID, new content). The old item is Archived. The new item inherits a lineage reference.
replacement_lineage.compound_key_role: The old item's QID is Archived (question_state: 'Archived'). A new item with a new QID is created. The new item's metadata records: replaced: 'P1-AD-001@20260724144500-1'. This preserves the audit trail of what content was superseded.
replacement_lineage.archival_protection: Archived items preserve all content fields (Stem, Choices, CC, EC, EW[A-D]). Only question_state changes to 'Archived'. The compound key remains resolvable in the registry — no loss of content provenance.

certification_history.description: Every state transition (Unprocessed → In Audit → Certified → In Audit → Certified → ...) is recorded in CERTIFICATION_LEDGER.json with the full compound key.
certification_history.audit_trail_integrity: Ledger is append-only. No entry is ever modified or deleted. The ledger holds full certification provenance for every item.

version_tracking.description: SHA-256 content hashing enables delta review: only items whose content changed since the last certification wave are reviewed. Unchanged items inherit their prior Quality verdict.
version_tracking.trigger: Content hash mismatch between current pack file extraction and DELTA_LEDGER.json baseline → item routes to full Quality Board review. Hash match → item skips review (unless overridden by scanner finding).

hash_computation.canonical_fields: Stem + Choices.{A,B,C,D} (sorted alphabetically) + CorrectChoice + ExplanationCorrect + ExplanationWrongA + ExplanationWrongB + ExplanationWrongC + ExplanationWrongD
hash_computation.canonical_serialization: JSON.stringify(fields, Object.keys(fields).sort()) — deterministic key ordering to ensure hash stability across extractors
hash_computation.metadata_hash_fields: Difficulty + DifficultyScore + CognitiveLevel + LOSTag + Topic + MicroTopic + UniqueConceptKey + question_state + certification_batch

delta_fingerprint.description: Every item in the Registered pool has a content fingerprint and a metadata fingerprint. These are stored in DELTA_LEDGER.json and refreshed after every certification wave. Fingerprints enable delta review — unchanged items skip re-review.

item_fingerprint.identity_key: SHA-256 of compound key string (without VersionID). Used for fast registry lookup. Stable across version changes.
item_fingerprint.content_hash: SHA-256 of canonical serialization of all learner-facing fields: Stem + Choices.{A,B,C,D} + CorrectChoice + ExplanationCorrect + ExplanationWrongA + ExplanationWrongB + ExplanationWrongC + ExplanationWrongD
item_fingerprint.metadata_hash: SHA-256 of Difficulty + DifficultyScore + CognitiveLevel + LOSTag + Topic + MicroTopic + UniqueConceptKey + question_state + certification_batch + certification_date

storage.format: JSON array of item_fingerprint objects, indexed by identity_key for O(1) lookup
storage.generation: Auto-generated from pack files at session T0 using AM-1 Function Constructor Parse. Never hand-edited.
storage.refresh: Updated after every certification wave that produces content changes. Only items with changed content_hash are updated. Unchanged items retain their prior fingerprint.

identity_resilience_checklist.description: How the identity model prevents each documented failure class. Every check maps to a specific defect class from DEFECT_LIBRARY.md.

preventions.failure_class: S320 — Variant Misidentification in Rotation Groups
preventions.how_prevented: Remediation scripts must target items by compound key (QID + CC + EW_Pattern + question_state), not QID alone. Within a rotation group, items are distinguished by CC value and EW_Pattern. A script targeting P1-EC-001 matches on CC=A AND EW_Pattern=0111 AND question_state='Unprocessed'. The first brace-delimited object containing 'P1-EC-001' is NOT assumed to be the canonical seed.
preventions.protocol: 1) Extract all items with QID prefix P1-EC-001 using within-object parse. 2) Filter by CC value. 3) Filter by EW_Pattern. 4) Filter by question_state. 5) If multiple matches remain, select the one with the most substantive EC (canonical seed selection). 6) If zero matches, escalate to human — no fallback to first-match.

preventions.failure_class: DL-029 — Forward-Scan CC-Offset False Positives (Pack B CC-before-QID format)
preventions.how_prevented: ALL scanners use AM-1 within-object extraction. The Function Constructor parse extracts each item's COMPLETE JSON object, including its own CorrectChoice and ExplanationWrong fields from the SAME object boundary. Pack B's CC-before-QID ordering is handled automatically by object-level extraction — no special CC-position logic needed.
preventions.protocol: 1) Parse pack file via Function constructor: const items = new Function(pack_source + '; return MCQ_BANK_X;')(). 2) For each item, read item.CorrectChoice and item.ExplanationWrong[A-D] from the same item object. 3) Never forward-scan from QuestionID to find CorrectChoice. Never use regex-window matching. 4) Pack B items produce correct CC through the function constructor — CC is extracted from the same object as QID regardless of field ordering.

preventions.failure_class: DL-016 — Metadata-Block vs. Content-Block Identity Divergence
preventions.how_prevented: The compound key's EW_Pattern + CorrectChoice pair is derived from the SAME object boundary as the Choices.{A,B,C,D} and Stem. There is no 'metadata block' vs 'content block' — the architecture handbook (SESSION201) clarifies this is a conceptual distinction within a single JSON object, not separate objects. The compound key fields are all at the top level of one brace-delimited entity.
preventions.protocol: 1) Extract the full JSON object for the item. 2) From that SINGLE object, read: CorrectChoice, ExplanationWrong[A-D], Choices.{A,B,C,D}, Stem, ExplanationCorrect. 3) Verify that EW[A] text semantically refers to Choices.A (choice-specific verification). 4) If EW[A] describes Choices.B or a different item's topic → flag DL-016. 5) Compound key fields (QID, CC, EW_Pattern, Template_Family) all come from the same object — no cross-object contamination possible.

preventions.failure_class: Cross-Pack QID Collision (Pack A Section E vs Pack E, Pack C vs Pack D template aliasing)
preventions.how_prevented: The File_Path component of the compound key disambiguates all cross-pack collisions. P1-E-042 in pack_a_corrected.js is a different item than P1E-E-042 in pack_e_corrected.js. P1-EC-001 in pack_c_corrected.js is a different item than P1-ED-001 in pack_d_corrected.js even though they share template families.
preventions.protocol: 1) Always include File_Path in compound key resolution. 2) QID alone is insufficient for cross-pack identity. 3) Registry Board maintains a global uniqueness constraint on the FULL compound key (QID + CC + EW_Pattern + File_Path). 4) Template_Family records cross-pack family relationships (Pack C and Pack D items in the same template family have different File_Path values but the same Template_Family identifier).

preventions.how_prevented: All scans use within-object extraction. The compound key's EW_Pattern field makes emptiness detection configuration-agnostic — a tool reporting DL-026 count must produce stable EW_Pattern fingerprints across runs. If fingerprints differ between scans, the scanner has a methodology error (e.g., brace-matcher undercount).
preventions.protocol: 1) Run scan twice with the same methodology. 2) Compare EW_Pattern fingerprints for each QID between runs. 3) If fingerprints differ → scanner methodology error (DL-020 brace-matcher string-awareness gap, or DL-029 CC-offset). 4) Do not accept any count that is not stable across two independent extraction passes.

registry_board_interface.description: The Registry Board manages the compound key namespace — the single source of truth for item identity. All other boards (Quality, Governance, Certification) query the Registry Board through this interface.

lookup.description: Find an item by any unique identifier. The registry supports multiple lookup modes for different use cases.

by_compound_key.output: Complete item fingerprint (content_hash, metadata_hash, question_state, certification_date, all quality scores, defect cross-references)

by_identity_key.output: Complete item fingerprint plus current VersionID. Identity_key is stable across version changes — used by delta review to find the item's prior baseline.

by_qid_within_file.input: QID + File_Path (partial key — finds all rotation variants)
by_qid_within_file.output: Array of all compound keys matching that QID+File_Path, sorted by VersionID desc. E.g., 'P1-AD-001' in pack_d_corrected.js returns AD-001 (CC=A, EW_Pattern=0111) and may return archived clones.
by_qid_within_file.use_case: Rotation group audit, canonical seed selection, clone identification.

by_template_family.output: Array of all compound keys in that family, including cross-pack siblings, with CC distribution and EW_Pattern distribution for rotation integrity verification.
by_template_family.use_case: Family-wide CorrectChoice audit, DL-030 sweep, clone archival verification.

insert.description: Register a new item or an existing item being enrolled in the compound key system. All 2,500 items must be registered (Phase 1 migration).
insert.input: Complete item fingerprint object (identity_key, content_hash, metadata_hash, compound_key, question_state, EW_Pattern)
preconditions: Compound key is globally unique (QID + CC + EW_Pattern + File_Path does not already exist in the ledger)
Content hash is computed from within-object AM-1 extraction (not regex scan)
EW_Pattern is verified against direct field-level inspection (not pattern-matching across object boundaries)
insert.output: Registered fingerprint with registry_entry_id (unique UUID), registered_date, registered_by (session ID)
insert.collision_handling: If compound key collision detected → escalate to human. Two items have the same QID, CC, EW_Pattern, and File_Path. This means either: (a) duplicate insert attempt (re-registering same item — safe to reject), or (b) genuine cross-pack collision (two different pack files with identical identity — check File_Path for pack-level disambiguation).

update.description: Update an item's fingerprint after a content change. The identity_key (without VersionID) remains stable. Only content_hash, metadata_hash, VersionID, and question_state change.
update.input: Existing identity_key + new fingerprint fields (content_hash, metadata_hash, VersionID, question_state, new EW_Pattern if applicable)
preconditions: The identity_key already exists in the ledger (item was previously registered)
The new content_hash differs from the stored content_hash (otherwise no update needed)
The EW_Pattern is verified post-write (confirms remediation was applied to the correct item variant)
Backup protocol completed before pack-file write (per BACKUP_PROTOCOL.md)
update.output: Updated fingerprint with previous_version set to old VersionID, last_updated timestamp, last_updated_by session ID
post_update_verification: Re-extract fingerprint from the pack file using AM-1 parse
Verify content_hash matches the computed hash from the updated pack file
Verify EW_Pattern matches the expected post-write signature
Verify CorrectChoice unchanged (unless answer-key change is explicitly authorized)
Verify QID count in pack file unchanged

collision_detection.description: Proactive collision detection at registry insertion, update, and session T0 reconciliation. Prevents compound-key duplication before it contaminates the delivery pool.
collision_detection.insert_time: At insertion: check identity_key against all existing ledger entries. Reject duplicate. Escalate if two different pack files produce the same identity_key (QID + CC + EW_Pattern + File_Path should be file-unique because File_Path embeds pack identity).
collision_detection.session_t0_reconciliation: At session startup: regenerate registry from pack files via AM-1 parse. Compare item count against prior session registry. If item count differs (items added or removed), reconcile through the G1-G5 gates. If compound key collision detected (two items produce identical identity_key), escalate — this indicates a registration methodology error.
collision_detection.cross_pack_family_verification: At registry generation: for all items sharing the same Template_Family but residing in different pack files (e.g., Pack C and Pack D items), verify that the Template_Family identifier is correctly cross-referenced. P1-EC-001 and P1-ED-001 are template siblings in different files — not collisions.
collision_detection.phantom_qid_detection: At session T0: cross-reference certified count from registry against dual-verified grep. If registry says 500 Certified but grep says 480, the registry is out of sync → re-generate from pack files.

steps.action: Generate compound key for all 2,500 items via AM-1 Function Constructor Parse
steps.output: registry entries for every item with QID, CC, EW_Pattern, File_Path, Template_Family

steps.action: Identify all template families via stem Jaccard similarity
steps.output: Template_Family assignments for all rotation-group items

steps.action: Compute SHA-256 content hashes for all 2,500 items
Independent re-extraction and re-hashing — 0 mismatches required
steps.output: Validation report confirming hash stability across two independent passes

steps.action: Backward-compatibility shim: QID-only lookup still works during transition. Quality Board agents that use QID-only are routed through the Registry Board which resolves QID + File_Path to the current active compound key (highest VersionID with non-Archived question_state).
steps.output: No existing tool breaks during transition. Old tools using QID-only continue functioning through the registry shim.

backward_compatibility.shim_behavior: A QID-only query (e.g., 'P1-AD-002' from the old scan tool) returns the first active (non-Archived) entry for that QID in the given File_Path, ordered by VersionID desc. If multiple active variants exist (same QID, different CC), the shim returns ALL matching variants with a warning: 'QID-only lookup returned multiple compound keys. Require CC or EW_Pattern to disambiguate.'
backward_compatibility.deprecation_schedule: QID-only lookup shim is active during Phase 1 (S202-S830). Deprecated in Phase 2 (S900+). All tools must use compound-key identity by S900.

governance_guard_extensions.description: Compound-Key Identity Required. No remediation script, certification entry, or question_state change may reference an item by QID alone from S830 onward. All item-level operations must use the full compound key or identity_key.
Registry Integrity. At session T0 and Tend, the registry must be regenerated from pack files and its item count must match dual-verified grep. Any discrepancy halts the session until resolved.

checks: Compound key uniqueness across all 2,500 items (no duplicate identity_key)
Template_Family completeness (all CC-rotation items assigned to a family)
Canonical seed viability (each family has at least one item meeting seed criteria)
Cross-pack QID collision audit (no two items with identical QID + File_Path but different CC → would be same item with conflicting identity)
EW_Pattern stability (identical across two independent AM-1 extraction passes)
VersionID uniqueness (no duplicate VersionIDs across all items)
